scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom used to host Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her kids and grandkids for about 50 years. Now she's too old, so we, the four kids, are supposed to take turns hosting. So far, each of us has hosted one holiday. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family is planning to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade. At first, it was just her sisters, but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet up there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event. And honestly, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He told me that our oldest sister is going to be really mad and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was upset. She said she'll probably end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom would be sad if I abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York. I offered to pay for them to rent a place and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother mentioned that his wife might be up for hosting, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't do it because she's renovating her house. I feel bad about backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions. I also offered to host the next holiday, but my oldest sister said no because it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that maybe me and him could swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here? I'm not sure. On one hand, I want to spend Thanksgiving with my wife's family, and it seems like a special opportunity. On the other hand, I'm supposed to be hosting this year, and my sister is upset because she feels like I'm not honoring our mom's wishes. I guess I need to think about what's more important: spending this time with my wife's family or keeping up with the tradition our mom started. Also, I need to consider how my actions are affecting my siblings and whether I'm being fair to them. Maybe I should talk to my brother and see if swapping Thanksgiving is feasible. If his wife is willing, that could solve the problem. But if not, then I might have to reconsider my plans with my wife's family. I also wonder if there's a way to compromise. Maybe we could go to the parade and still have a smaller Thanksgiving gathering with my siblings. Or perhaps we could adjust our plans to accommodate both traditions. It's a tough situation because I don't want to upset my sister or break the tradition, but I also don't want to miss out on this special event with my wife and daughter. I need to find a balance that works for everyone involved. Maybe I should also talk to my mom and see how she feels about this. She might have some advice or a different perspective that could help me make the right decision. Overall, I think I need to weigh the importance of family traditions against the opportunity to create new memories with my wife's family. It's not easy, and I might not get it perfect, but I need to make a decision that I feel is fair to everyone.
